texts: mixed: everything is captured and the rule fires, but the trigger is a state ("a winter night IS clear") rather than a happening, so there is no occurrence for the consequence to be timed against and the wind's coming ends up hung on the night itself — a corner the instruction set does not settle. Make the trigger an event, as your third sentence already does: "Whenever a clear winter night falls, the cold-threshold wind comes off the Cold Sea."

mixed: the rule fires and says the right thing, but "that mire-essence" points back at a bare substance word, which is normally treated as the stuff in general and not as a particular quantity, so there is nothing licensed for the demonstrative to pick out; the parse individuates the mire-essence anyway while leaving the salt-bloom generic, an improvisation another run may not repeat. Give the thing that burns a countable phrase so the pointer has a real antecedent: "Whenever a Keeper mixes salt-bloom into a batch of mire-essence, that batch of mire-essence burns slowly."

good. one rule covers both quantifications — every arrival of a cold-threshold night, and every unprepared lantern on the Cliff Path — with the dying tied to the night that triggered it and the Cliff Path recorded as a named place the lanterns sit on.
